title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — 28 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart, and its biomedical coverage is incomplete; this is an inferred relevance ranking from one batch, not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Thirty unique arXiv IDs appeared across the configured category listings for the latest batch; twelve are highlighted. Protein–glycan modelling, biomolecular simulation, RNA data resources and genomics methods form the strongest biology-centered threads. The current day’s batch had not yet been announced, so this uses the prior batch dated 28 October.

sections.title: Accurate structural modelling of protein-glycan recognition with GlycoWeave
sections.abstract: GlycoWeave uses chemically constrained diffusion and multiscale representations to predict protein–glycan complex structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports 71.9% Top-25 high-quality success across 698 complexes versus 19.2% for AlphaFold 3, with 0.34 seconds per sampled pose.
sections.unique_caveat: In-silico structural comparisons do not establish binding affinity, biological function, or clinical utility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 698-complex structural benchmark and explicit AlphaFold 3 comparator.

sections.title: A unified coarse-grained neural network potential for the dynamics of biomolecular complexes
sections.abstract: AMARO v2.0 is a shared heavy-atom coarse-grained neural potential for protein, ligand and ternary biomolecular-complex dynamics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 262 complexes across 11 targets and a 3.3-fold increase in trajectories reaching the trypsin–benzamidine crystal pose versus all-atom mechanics at fixed estimated GPU time.
sections.unique_caveat: Free-energy estimates are more favorable than experimental references; reported failure cases include SHP2, CDK8 and HIF2A complex behavior.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Tests span 262 complexes and 11 targets with targeted all-atom comparisons.

sections.title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
sections.abstract: mdRNAcat provides standardized coordinates, forces, structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata from enhanced-sampling simulations of 48 RNA systems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a homogeneous HDF5 resource with coordinates, instantaneous forces and reference-Hamiltonian forces across 48 systems and 32 REST2 states per system; total simulated time is 316.8 microseconds.
sections.unique_caveat: These are simulations rather than experimental native ensembles; elevated-temperature samples require care in thermodynamic interpretation, and the dataset is about 699 GB.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A substantive v2 revision in this batch, broad RNA resource, and three relevant categories.

sections.title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
sections.abstract: Sparse autoencoders and attribution are used to interpret how ESMFold’s internal representations build predicted protein geometry.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint proposes an interpretable account of the ESMFold trunk’s single- and pair-representation computations and reports feature activations predictive of the model’s own fold quality.
sections.unique_caveat: Internal-model interpretation is not experimental validation of biological mechanisms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Traces learned features across model blocks to folding outputs and connects them to biochemical interpretations.

sections.title: HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching
sections.abstract: HELICS learns conditional generation of genome-wide common-variant genotypes from biobank-scale data using latent flow matching.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports phasing-free synthesis across more than 600,000 SNPs, trained on more than 417,000 UK Biobank genomes, with external allele-frequency and correlation fidelity checks.
sections.unique_caveat: Synthetic genotype fidelity is not a formal privacy guarantee or proof of downstream disease-prediction utility; liability conditioning is not clinical evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large biobank training set and external genotype-fidelity evaluation.

sections.title: ACOR: incremental evidence accumulation towards real-time DNA storage reconstruction
sections.abstract: ACOR incrementally accumulates k-mer evidence and reconstructs consensus sequences as assigned DNA-storage reads arrive.
sections.claimed_contribution: In a wet-lab NGS library of 96,055 designs and about 17.7 million assigned observations, the k=15 run reports 99.9844% exact recovery in 20.5 seconds.
sections.unique_caveat: It reconstructs already assigned read clusters rather than the full end-to-end sequencing, clustering and decoding pipeline; runtime depends on hardware and configuration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Real wet-lab library plus public and simulated DNA-storage data.

sections.title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data
sections.abstract: The authors evaluate out-of-distribution detection for DNA-methylation tumor classifiers across sarcoma and brain-tumor data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint reports mean AUROC 0.976 and TNR 0.935 on an independent clinical dataset and proposes OOD detection as a classifier quality-control layer.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective evaluation does not establish prospective diagnostic validity or improved patient outcomes; the abstract does not state test-set size.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reported cross-validation, held-out samples and an independent clinical test set.

sections.title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
sections.abstract: HGPRGDel ranks candidate gene deletions for microbial growth-coupled production while representing gene–protein–reaction logic.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across three metabolic models, the authors report the best macro-F1 and AUC among evaluated configurations and recovery of an average 90% of reference deletion genes while examining fewer candidates.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are computational against curated/reference designs; no engineered-strain experiments or metabolite measurements are reported in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three metabolic models and comparison with baseline prioritization methods.

sections.title: pyTransRate: 1 reference-free quality assessment of de novo transcriptome assemblies with current aligners and quantifiers
sections.abstract: pyTransRate reimplements reference-free transcriptome-assembly scoring with current alignment and quantification software.
sections.claimed_contribution: In 5,031 comparisons across 129 public assemblies, the author reports Spearman correlations of 0.94 for assembly score and 0.98 for good-mapping rate against TransRate 1.0.3.
sections.unique_caveat: Read-based scores are not numerically interchangeable with the older implementation, and agreement with legacy software is not an independent measure of assembly truth.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A 129-assembly reproducibility comparison and maintained workflow dependencies.

sections.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
sections.abstract: OpenGray tests whether radiotherapy-planning agents correctly submit, revise or escalate plans when dose goals are contradictory or feasible.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a decision benchmark on 30 patients and analysis of logs from 39 stereotactic radiosurgery runs, highlighting failures concealed by aggregate dose scores.
sections.unique_caveat: A small benchmark and retrospective logs do not establish safety or effectiveness in clinical practice.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four systems are tested against contradiction and feasible-control tasks with known answers.

sections.title: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework
sections.abstract: The authors estimate the myelin-sensitive macromolecular pool fraction from conventional brain MRI using a physics-guided self-supervised model.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint proposes MPF mapping from T1-, T2- and FLAIR-weighted scans without paired quantitative-reference scans and reports 7,705 sessions overall with 1,237 test sessions.
sections.unique_caveat: Lesion contrast is a retrospective association, not a validated diagnostic test or clinical outcome; the demyelinating-disease subset is 70 sessions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Multisite, multivendor dataset with 1,237 test sessions and a reported lesion-versus-normal-appearing-white-matter contrast.

sections.title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
sections.abstract: The authors measure proton-induced technetium-isotope production cross-sections from molybdenum targets to optimize a cyclotron route to 99mTc.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report production tests and a calculated yield of about 1.7 GBq/μA for a 10-hour irradiation using a 16 MeV proton beam and a 0.5 mm highly enriched 100Mo target.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated activity is a calculated yield from measured data and production tests, not evidence of routine commercial-scale supply or clinical outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Measured cross-sections and production tests are reported, alongside stated purity limits.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Chemistry-aware molecular modelling appears in GlycoWeave, AMARO and ESMFold interpretability. mdRNAcat contributes simulated RNA ensembles. HELICS, methylation OOD and ACOR address distinct genomic-data tasks. HGPRGDel, pyTransRate, OpenGray, MPF mapping and 99mTc production have different evidence types and do not collectively establish clinical benefit.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Follow molecular predictions with blinded biochemical or structural tests; compare RNA ensemble models with experimental restraints; evaluate synthetic-genome privacy and utility separately; test DNA-storage reconstruction end to end; validate methylation and MPF methods prospectively across institutions; enlarge radiotherapy-agent benchmarks; and measure predicted metabolic-engineering strategies in wet-lab strains.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This batch is strongest in computational molecular structure, RNA simulation resources and genomics methods, with biomedical studies anchored by clinical-image datasets or measured production cross-sections. Reported validation is promising but uneven; no paper supports a practice-changing clinical claim, and evidence does not justify calling the batch trending by readership.
